articles.title: Premier League incident-by-incident: Was it a bad weekend for VAR?
articles.summary: Almost every game had a controversial VAR decision in the Premier League this weekend. But how many might go down as errors?
articles.body:
Whisper it quietly, but the statistics say video assistant referee decisions have been pretty good in the Premier League so far this season.

The Key Match Incidents (KMI) Panel, which looks at every contentious decision and votes whether it is right or wrong, reported just two VAR errors after eight rounds of matches.

At the same stage last season, there had been six mistakes.

Then came this weekend, during which almost every top-flight game had a controversial decision.

BBC Sport looks at most of these situations - there really were too many to do them all - and assesses the likelihood that the KMI Panel will add to the list of errors.

Incident 1: Penalty awarded to Manchester United for a foul by Boubacar Kamara on Matheus Cunha in the 16th minute.

Verdict: The spot-kick was awarded because the Villa defender went through Cunha to win the ball. Replays clearly showed the first contact was on the Brazilian's foot.

What the KMI Panel might say: This will be a correct decision.

Incident 2: Possible foul by Senne Lammens on Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki before Patrick Dorgu's 96th-minute equaliser.

Verdict : There are similarities to a goal Arsenal scored at Old Trafford last season, when William Saliba leant into United goalkeeper Altay Bayındır.

Lammens was not looking at the ball, which increases the chances of a VAR intervention.

What the KMI Panel might say: With the higher bar for an intervention in the Premier League, and minimal contact, it is unlikely to be a VAR error to not disallow the goal.

Incident: Kai Havertz was pulled down inside the area by Nobel Mendy. The VAR, Michael Oliver, sent referee Farai Hallam to the pitchside monitor for a penalty, but it was not given due to an offside offence by the Germany international.

Verdict: BBC Sport covered this incident in detail on Saturday . As the foul happened before any potential offside offence, the penalty should have been awarded.

What the KMI Panel might say: Even though it feels wrong to reward a player in an offside position with a penalty, the law says otherwise and this is likely to be a mistake.

Incident: Jayden Bogle fouled Mathys Tel, with referee John Brooks giving the free-kick but no sanction for the Leeds player. The VAR, Tony Harrington, opted not to send Brooks to the monitor for a red card.

Verdict: BBC Sport covered the merits of this incident on Saturday . It was a difficult call for the VAR, because Bogle caused the foul with his supporting rather than his challenging foot. Still, it was a very painful challenge and some believe it should have been a red card.

What the KMI Panel might say: Was it an unfortunate incident, or a tackle which endangered the opponent? This will depend upon which former players are on the KMI Panel for this week, because it has split opinion among ex-pros.

All three incidents were covered in more detail by BBC Sport on Friday.

Incident 1: Coventry 's Caleb Yirenkyi appeared to have his hair pulled inside the area by James Tarkowski, but no penalty was awarded.

Verdict: While the interpretation on hair pulling was relaxed for this season, meaning this would not be a red card, there appeared to be a yank of the hair by the Everton defender.

What the KMI Panel might say: Incorrect decision, penalty kick.

Incident 2: Another penalty claim for Coventry as Everton 's Vitalii Mykolenko clipped Taiwo Awoniyi on the edge of the box.

Verdict: Replays shows that the contact on Awoniyi was made just before the line.

What the KMI Panel might say: Correct decision, no penalty.

Incident 3: Thierno Barry put Everton in front in the 61st minute, but there was a VAR check for a potential handball.

Verdict: The VAR determined there was no conclusive evidence for a handball, yet there does appear to be a deviation and the goal probably should have been ruled out.

What the KMI Panel might say: As the VAR does not have the super-zoom - this takes a few minutes to calibrate and is not available instantly - no VAR intervention might be supported. This was the case with a goal scored by Crystal Palace against Nottingham Forest . It could be a split vote.

Incident: Igor Thiago was sent off following a VAR review after he caught the head of Chema Andres with his forearm.

Verdict: The Brentford striker can consider himself unfortunate, as there is doubt that he truly intended to catch the Spaniard in the face.

What the KMI Panel might say: It may seem like a soft dismissal, but the VAR intervention is likely to be supported because the law does say that a strike to the head should be a red card, unless force is negligible.

Incident: Crystal Palace were awarded a penalty three minutes into stoppage time for a foul by Milos Kerkez on Dario Osorio.

Verdict: We saw a similar incident the 2024-25 season when Arsenal defender William Saliba headed Joao Pedro after the Brighton striker had won the ball. This was voted to be a correct penalty decision.

What the KMI Panel might say: This incident is not quite the same as Saliba on Pedro, and more of a 50-50 clash. It may be voted as an on-field error, but not to the threshold for VAR.

Incident: Cole Palmer went down on the edge of the area under a challenge from both Luke O'Nien and Jules Ahoka, and asked for a penalty. Referee Jarred Gillett did not give a foul.

Verdict: A foul is determined by the first contact on the attacker. That a player falls into the box with contact continuing would not make it a penalty. Only on holding offences is continuing contact relevant.

What the KMI Panel might say: There is no conclusive evidence that any initial foul contact happened inside the area, so no penalty is likely to be supported.

Incident: Newcastle thought they had taken the lead at Craven Cottage, only for the goal to be ruled out for a foul by Yoane Wissa on Timothy Castagne.

Verdict: Matthias Jaissle was perplexed in his post-match interview, yet he would surely be furious if a Fulham player held one of his defenders back to create on onside corridor for another attacker to score.

What the KMI Panel might say: This is likely to be voted as a correct decision.

BBC Sport estimates that there are two decisions which the KMI Panel is very likely to log as a VAR error: not awarding penalties to Arsenal and Coventry .

Two further calls, Barry's goal and the potential red card to Bogle, may be errors but will depend who is on the panel and where their subjective opinion lies.

The others on the list are likely to be correct.

So we are potentially looking at two to four errors, which is not a good weekend.

articles.title: Kettering Town says it 'cannot hide' from its racism problem
articles.summary: Kettering Town says it "can no longer hide" from the issue of racism after a visiting Redditch player was allegedly subjected to "sickening" abuse.
articles.body:
Non-league Kettering Town have said they "can no longer hide" from the issue of racism after a visiting player was allegedly subjected to "sickening" abuse.

Redditch United player Dan Sweeney said he was targeted by a Kettering supporter during Saturday's Southern League Premier Division Central tie at the Poppies' Latimer Park stadium, which the hosts won 2-1.

In a statement, Kettering director of football Fabian Forde said the "poison" of racism went beyond matchdays.

He also spoke out against the presence of what he called "festering" racism on the club's fans forums.

Writing on the club's website , external , Forde said: "Let's be completely honest with ourselves: this is not the first time. We can no longer hide behind the comforting lie that 'it's just a small minority' or 'they don't reflect the majority of our fans'.

"Every single time we dismiss hate by calling it a minority issue, we minimise the damage. The truth is, if the majority stays silent, that small minority becomes our identity.

"They tarnish our reputation in the eyes of opposition players, fans, and officials. They make our club look like a haven for bigotry. Is that really who we want to be?"

Forde added that the club could not "keep sending out generic statements that mean nothing" and urged fans to support "real cultural change" by taking responsibility for calling out the perpetrators of racist abuse.

He said: "To the majority of our fans, the good, decent people who love this club for the right reasons, we are pleading with you.

"We need you to stand up. We need you to confront this minority head-on. If you see someone typing hate online, call them out. If you hear someone shouting abuse next to you on a Saturday afternoon, don't look away.

"Tell a steward. Identify them to the club. Why are we protecting people who are actively destroying the reputation of the club we love?"

Northamptonshire Police said they had "not identified any report relating to this [Saturday's] allegation."

However, the force added: "It may be that any report is awaiting allocation or has been made to another police force. Should a report be made elsewhere and the alleged offence be found to have taken place within Northamptonshire, we would take ownership of the investigation.

"We note Kettering Town FC's statement that it is working with its security team, stewards and the relevant authorities to identify those responsible, and we would encourage anyone who believes they have been the victim of a crime to report it to police.

"Racial abuse has no place in football or wider society, and any reports made to us will be assessed and investigated appropriately."

In a statement , external , Redditch United chairman David Faulkner said: "I particularly welcome Kettering Town's commitment to working with its security team, stewards and the relevant authorities to identify those responsible.

"It is vital that this matter is taken seriously and that appropriate action follows.

"Tackling racism requires more than statements. It requires leadership, accountability and a collective willingness to challenge unacceptable behaviour whenever and wherever it occurs.

"We must never allow incidents like this to become normalised, dismissed or simply forgotten once the immediate attention has passed."

The Football Association has also been approached for comment.

articles.title: Alabama's Josh Ford Injured, Latest Rumors on Surgery Decision and TE's Status for 2026 Season
articles.summary: Alabama was riding high after Saturday's 31-13 win over rival LSU, but the wind has been taken out of their sails.
articles.body:
Alabama was riding high after Saturday's 31-13 win over rival LSU, but the wind has been taken out of their sails.

Pete Nakos of On3.com reported on Monday that Crimson Tide tight end Josh Ford suffered a season-ending injury and is expected to undergo surgery later this week. He had recorded two catches for 15 yards and a touchdown against the Tigers on Saturday before exiting the game early.

Ford ends the 2026 season with five catches for 41 yards and two touchdowns. He spent his first two collegiate seasons at Oklahoma State and has career numbers of 18 receptions, 178 yards and four scores.

Nakos noted that before Saturday's season-ending injury, Ford showed incredible toughness by playing through a broken forearm suffered in October. He underwent surgery but managed to quickly return to the field.

"It's still recovering, but I couldn't do it without them, that's for sure," Ford said of his surgeon and Alabama's medical staff. "Saturday, it was my decision to play or not. They weren't forcing me out there. But I felt good to go, and they made a carbon-fiber plate. It's dang near invincible."

While losing Ford stings, the Crimson Tide have a pair of talented tight ends in Marshall Pritchett and Kaleb Edwards, who have combined for five touchdowns this season.

Alabama (7-2) was ranked No. 5 in last week's College Football Playoff poll, so Saturday's win could help the Crimson Tide rise this week. The team will try to keep the momentum going when it faces Vanderbilt (4-5) on Saturday.

articles.title: Fifpro Women's World 11: Lucy Bronze selected for record ninth time
articles.summary: Lucy Bronze is one of five England players named in the Fifpro Women's World 11.
articles.body:
England defender Lucy Bronze has been named in the Fifpro Women's World 11 for a record ninth time.

Bronze is one of five England players named, with Alex Greenwood, Alessia Russo, Ella Toone and Hannah Hampton also selected.

Spain defender Irene Paredes also features for the first time since her previous selection in 2017.

Zambia striker Barbra Banda, named in the team for the third time, is the only player in the side based outside England or Spain.

The World 11 - the only global football award chosen exclusively by players - was selected through votes from 6,511 female players from 64 countries.

Goalkeeper: Hannah Hampton (Chelsea, England).

Defenders: Lucy Bronze (Chelsea, England), Alex Greenwood (Manchester City, England), Mapi Leon (Barcelona/London City Lionesses, Spain), Irene Paredes (Barcelona, Spain).

Midfielders: Aitana Bonmati (Barcelona, Spain), Alexia Putellas (Barcelona/London City Lionesses, Spain), Ella Toone (Manchester United, England)

Forwards: Barbra Banda (Orlando Pride, Zambia), Claudia Pina (Barcelona, Spain), Alessia Russo (Arsenal, England)

Professional players voted based on performances between 4 August 2025 and 16 August 2026, with only those with at least 20 appearances eligible.

Voters were asked to choose the three players who had performed best in each position: goalkeeper, defender, midfielder and forward.

The goalkeeper, three defenders, three midfielders and three forwards who received the most votes were selected for the World 11.

The final place was awarded to the outfield player with the next highest overall vote total, regardless of position.

articles.title: Manchester United: The key questions with Michael Carrick's future still up in the air at Old Trafford
articles.summary: Michael Carrick insists he expects to be in charge when Manchester United return from the international break; his side came from two goals behind on three occasions in the last two games alone; United sit 18th in the Premier League and face Liverpool at Anfield next
articles.body:
Ahead of what is bound to be a pivotal international break for Carrick's tenure , Sky Sports answers the key questions surrounding the state of play at Old Trafford.

Do Man Utd bosses know where to go with Carrick?

It's unclear if Manchester United's bosses know exactly where they go from here. They will not rush a decision over Carrick's future.

For several weeks, they have been assessing exactly that and considering whether or not to make a change, but they haven't made a decision yet.

Sky Sports News understands the club's hierarchy are planning to use the international break to fully evaluate the season so far and reassess their options.

The season on a whole has been an absolute disaster. One win in 11 - their worst ever start to a Premier League campaign. They're in the relegation zone. They have conceded 30 goals in all competitions this season, the second-most of all teams in Europe's top five leagues.

The question now is: did that comeback, did the character they showed for the second game on the trot after the comeback win over Roma , show that the players are enough behind Carrick for him to keep his job?

A fortnight ago, when Manchester United lost 3-0 at home to Bournemouth, it was suspected that was the end of the Carrick era. There were a lot of people within the club suggesting that was the feeling on the inside.

The hierarchy didn't come out and publicly back him. They decided to stick with the status quo. Sky Sports News' understanding is that they were trying to get through to this international break, where they would make a full reassessment.

It still feels that Carrick is incredibly vulnerable as Manchester United boss. The hierarchy have the time now. The team don't play a game for two weeks, where they could make a change. They could do their due diligence and start talking to alternative candidates should they want to.

However, the ideal scenario for Man Utd bosses is to try and keep Carrick in his job until the end of the season.

Who are the targets if Carrick is sacked?

If they do sack Carrick, they won't appoint another interim. They don't want to get caught in a cycle where they appoint an interim until the end of the season, that manager does exactly what Carrick did last season and does incredibly well, the fanbase get behind them and clamour for that person to get the job on a permanent basis and then they are right back to square one.

Whether or not this is achievable, the bosses are determined to try and get a long-term strategy and a long-term head coach in place. If that's not Carrick, they don't know who that is.

We know they are interested in Julian Nagelsmann. We know they are interested in Eddie Howe. We know they are interested in Fabian Hurzeler at Brighton who is doing an incredible job. But they aren't solely committed to those right now.

Unai Emery was very high up on those lists of potential targets. That's why we saw that massive PR show from Aston Villa chairman Nassef Sawiris, who said 'he's one of our own. We've got a long-term plan, he's going to sign a new contract'. That's where we are at with Aston Villa. It's unlikely United can get Emery out of Aston Villa.

You can't rule it out forever, but you likely can for now. It is very clear that Aston Villa do not want and will not let their manager go anywhere. Emery still has a contract that ties him to the football club until 2029. He's pretty secure as far as the Aston Villa ownership is concerned.

Clearly defensively. The 30 goals they have conceded is abhorrent. Conceding four goals at home to Aston Villa that haven't won at Old Trafford in more than a century is abhorrent.

Manchester United massively outperformed last season in finishing third and getting Champions League football. This season, they have massively underperformed with the squad that they've got. Somewhere between the two is probably about right.

Carrick did such a fantastic job last season that he built up the expectation that United would go forward and would improve from there.

They're creating chances. They're scoring goals. They've scored seven in their last two games, but shipped six. So, that defensive record is a real concern for Man Utd right now.

It's a really strange atmosphere around Old Trafford. Lisandro Martinez came out a few weeks ago and criticised the board for their lack of recruitment and lack of ambition. The next game, he was cheered by Manchester United supporters for saying that.

Carrick is cheered off like a hero after the loss to Bournemouth and fans probably expected him to be sacked based on the run of results. There is affection for the manager still.

We then saw an awful lot before the Villa game from the stands. There were green and yellow balloons let off in protest at the ownership and the Glazers, accompanied by banners demanding they leave the club.

The truth is, Manchester United supporters don't know what to make of this right now. Who to cheer and who to boo. They are ashamed and at a loss as to where to go from here. I think at the moment, that's a feeling matched in the boardroom.

Are there any plans for the January window?

A clear weakness of Manchester United's side this season has been at left-back. They have had five different players take up that position this season with limited success, especially since Luke Shaw's injury.

It was a position they wanted to strengthen in the summer but decided to sign an extra midfielder instead. Expect them to explore that area again in January with perhaps a revisit to Manchester City's Rayan Ait-Nouri , who is getting limited game time under Enzo Maresca this season.

United were also looking for a forward but it remains to be seen whether their January budget will allow them to strengthen in both areas. Any significant incomings will also be dictated by departures but looking at United's squad, it's difficult to see many players leaving aside from fringe players such as Harry Amass .

Joshua Zirkzee is one who could leave but has also proven how useful he can be off the bench with a key goal against Aston Villa.

Can Carrick get a pass if Palace sack Sage?

Those outside Old Trafford will ponder what the difference between Manchester United and Crystal Palace is as things stand? While one head coach is likely out at Selhurst Park, their counterpart at United still has a chance of staying despite their positions being so close in the table and more importantly, in the relegation zone.

There is no clear answer, clearly. But, if you deem Carrick the problem, the issue the hierarchy has is who is the solution?

His connection to the fanbase is unique. One Sage does not have with Crystal Palace for obvious reasons.

Carrick is also seen as a great custodian of the club in terms of how he presents himself in the media and how he has handled the many challenges thrown at him this season. All of these aspects have to be considered in comparison to thinking a coach can just slot straight in at Crystal Palace.

The last time they won a league game, the schools were still closed for summer holidays. The transfer window was still open.

The sides that are below them have won twice as many games. They are picking up 0.8 points per game. Across a whole season, it means they will pick up 30 points. That is guaranteed relegation.

The last time they were relegated, they actually had a better start to the season than they have had this time around. I know some people are saying it is business as usual. But, business as usual means relegation unless there are big changes at the club.
authors: Rob Dorsett, Danyal Khan and Kaveh Solhekol

articles.title: Fantasy Football Stock Report: Jordan Love on a heater while Lions' depth receivers struggle coming out of Week 9
articles.summary: Matt Okada takes you through some of his top risers and fallers for fantasy football going into Week 10.
articles.body:
As I write this on Sunday night, 14 of 15 Week 9 games are in the books (with Monday night remaining) and the fantasy football season is now past the halfway point. Still, things are changing every week. Promising improvements. Concerning trends. Performances that change our early outlook on players and teams. As always, some of these shifting perspectives will have permanent ramifications in fantasy football.

With that in mind, I've compiled another full fantasy stock report. These are the most notable risers and fallers heading into Week 10.

QB C.J. Stroud & Wide Receivers, Houston Texans

I confess, I did not love C.J. Stroud for this Sunday, given how tough the Chargers had been against quarterbacks. My bad.

Stroud had one of his best games as a pro, throwing for 384 yards and five touchdowns (with one INT), plus 20 rushing yards just for kicks. His 36.36 fantasy points were the second-most of his career ... and it wasn't an aberration. Stroud now has 20+ fantasy points in four of his last five games and is averaging 24.18 PPG over that span. A big part of the story: Tank Dell's breakout after a multi-year absence and a monster game from Kayshon Boutte. Nico Collins also had 55 yards and a TD, but it was Boutte's 4-125-2 and Dell's 4-105-1 that really made the difference (oh, and Xavier Hutchinson snagged a TD as well).

This is an eclectic, but clearly talented, receiving corps and Stroud is making it work to his advantage (and that of his fantasy managers). Dell is a great waiver wire add — and/or Boutte in deeper leagues — and Stroud might be a strong trade target before your league's deadline, considering he might be another manager's QB2.

Speaking of monster quarterback performances, Jordan Love might be the hottest QB in the league right now. He looked unstoppable on Sunday against the Patriots, completing 23 of 29 passes for 372 yards and three touchdowns, for a 153.2 passer rating and 36.18 fantasy points. He's now topped 21 points in four of his last five games — with 17.96 in the fifth — and is averaging 24.04 points per game over that span.

The connections with Christian Watson and Matthew Golden are both exquisite right now, as arguably the only trio playing better is Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins for the Bengals ... and it's close. Over the entire season, Love has thrown for fewer than 270 yards just twice, both in the first month. His 2,618 passing yards lead the league and have him on pace for — double-checks math — 4,945 yards on the year. Now, of course, the ultimate test comes next week against the Vikings — I would frankly consider sitting him despite the red-hot stretch against this Minnesota defense — and then Love has his bye in Week 11. But with a playoff stretch that includes the Bills, Dolphins, Bears and Texans, Love could be pretty well positioned to win fantasy managers a title in 2026.

Jonah Coleman was the hottest name in fantasy the past week — I called him the waiver-wire pickup of the year on air — and he did not disappoint in Week 9. Despite surprising inefficiency on the ground — considering the matchup with Carolina — Coleman totaled 88 scrimmage yards (with four catches) and a nine-yard touchdown run in the fourth quarter. He played a whopping 81.5% of the snaps and handled 81% of the running back carries, putting to bed any lingering concerns about J.K. Dobbins "vulturizing" the rookie (yes, I just made that word up). That's not just "head-of-the-committee" volume, that's true bell-cow volume. Yes, it's possible that when RJ Harvey eventually returns from IR, Coleman might lose a bit of his receiving upside, but that's weeks away. It's also possible the Broncos trade for a running back (Jonathan Taylor?) ... and that might be hours away, depending on when you read this. But hopefully that doesn't happen.

As long as Coleman makes it through Tuesday afternoon as the RB1, he's going to be a league-winner down the stretch. Congratulations if you picked him, kudos if you drafted him and if you're in neither of those positions and can trade for him on Tuesday at 4:01 p.m. ET, do it.

Frankly, Breece Hall just needed to make it back to the field for his Stock to be Up after a five-week absence. But he did more than that, out-carrying Braelon Allen 15-to-8, matching Allen's 4.1 yards per carry and slightly outperforming him as a receiver (with three catches for 26 yards). Given how well Allen had played in Hall's stead, there was some realistic concern that he would be relegated to a pass-catching role or to a distant No. 2 slot in a frustrating committee.

Hall did trail Allen in snap share (43.5% to 58.1%), but that's likely a side effect of the Jets easing Hall back into action. As long as neither back is moved at the trade deadline — which should reportedly be the case — I'd expect Hall to retake the lead in snap share and for his fantasy production to reflect that moving forward. Allen has played well enough that Hall's once-upon-a-time bell-cow workload is probably a thing of the past, but 19 opportunities in his first game back — in a game the Jets lost 35-12, by the way — is extremely encouraging. He should be a strong RB2 moving forward.

In this week's version of the ongoing "Which 49ers Wide Receiver Do We Like?" mini-game, it was Jordan Watkins who stepped up big to the tune of four catches for 86 yards and a touchdown. He's now topped 50 receiving yards in three of the four games he's played this season and is averaging 22.4 yards per reception this season. Dig a little deeper and you get this nugget: Watkins leads all players with 100+ routes run in yards per target at 17.2.

And while he hadn't been consistently involved enough for that to matter much earlier in the year, he led San Francisco with 26 routes on Sunday and tied George Kittle for the team high in catches. Obviously, Mike Evans will return soon and Watkins will drop to the WR2 spot at best , with Kittle and Christian McCaffrey also heavily involved. However, as we've seen with Brock Purdy at the helm, there is room for fantasy goodness a ways down this depth chart. Watkins should be heavily added off waivers, and if Evans struggles to return or stay healthy, he might have weekly starter upside down the stretch.

Kyren Williams had stayed strong for fantasy amid the rise of Blake Corum by finding the end zone more often than not. Without that TD in Week 9, the Rams RB1A — theoretically — scored just 7.6 points on 61 scrimmage yards. It's his second game with single-digit fantasy points over the last month, and Williams has averaged just 11.3 PPG over that stretch after scoring 19.2 PPG over the first five weeks. And while he did play more snaps and out-carried Corum 15-to-11 on Sunday, the latter back was far more efficient, logging 5.3 yards per carry and scoring the goal-line touchdown , while Williams clocked in at just 3.0 yards per carry.

Williams is still a borderline must-start — you'd have to be stocked at running back to sit him in any given week — but the ceiling has been clearly and noticeably lowered with Corum's ongoing involvement (especially in the red zone). If you can get low-end RB1 (or even high-end RB2) value for Williams in a trade, it might not be a terrible idea.

I very actively and vocally disliked Ollie Gordon II in this matchup with the Lions' pass-funnel defense, so the 6.9 fantasy points on an inefficient 17 touches doesn't surprise me. That said, it was his second consecutive game with exactly 6.9 points and has clearly revealed the weakness in Gordon's game: he has no receiving upside (23 total receiving yards on the year) and is not dominant enough to beat strong run defenses. That means that, from week-to-week, Gordon's ceiling is going to depend heavily on touchdowns and opposing defenses.

The good news there is that his remaining schedule is relatively soft, so it's possible we see more "good Gordon" than "meh Gordon" down the stretch. The bad news is that there is a clear cap on his fantasy upside: even in his great outings, Gordon still hasn't scored more than 17 fantasy points in a game this season. He's a low-end RB2 with a high(ish) volume-based floor, but he's still a relatively average back in the Miami Dolphins offense.

TE Sam LaPorta & WR Jameson Williams, Detroit Lions

While Amon-Ra St. Brown was excellent and Jahmyr Gibbs was good enough on Sunday, Sam LaPorta had another fantasy dud and Jameson Williams came crashing back to earth. LaPorta now has fewer than six fantasy points in three straight games and is averaging just 4.2 points per game since the Week 6 bye. It's been a strange change of fortunes after he scored 14+ in three of four weeks heading into the bye, and it was particularly discouraging in what has been a great tight-end matchup with Miami.

As for Williams, he finally did the Jameson Williams thing — after four straight excellent games, with 13+ fantasy points in each, he logged a 4.5-point dud with just one catch (and one rush) all day. The matchup was much worse for Williams than for LaPorta, so we'll give him a little grace there, but this was a stark and long-awaited reminder that Williams is prone to disappear every now and then.

By all accounts, Goff and Co. should bounce back in future weeks, though they do have the Patriots on deck, the Buccaneers in the hole and another meeting with the Vikings in Week 15. Just keep in mind: this offense runs through Gibbs and St. Brown, and everyone else will have down days.

In his first five games with Michael Penix Jr. this year, Drake London averaged 6.4 receptions and 107.2 receiving yards per game ... and scored his lone touchdown of the year. Over the last two weeks, London has six catches and 76 receiving yards combined . He had seen 10+ targets in four of those first five games and has now seen just 11 total targets these last two games. This was his fourth straight game with fewer than 70 receiving yards, and while that's a relatively high bar, his lack of touchdowns requires massive yardage to compensate for fantasy. For reference, every other player with at least 480 receiving yards has multiple touchdown receptions this season — London has 692 yards (eighth in the league) and just one score.

To make matters worse, London's next three weeks are just about as bad as you can get: the Chiefs, the bye, the Vikings. Even if he does return to WR1 upside in December or so, London is entering an extremely ugly stretch. If you can, try to trade him for a more consistent WR1 — maybe Tee Higgins — before a couple more duds or your league's trade deadline make him unmovable.

articles.title: Los 9, señalados
articles.standfirst: Los delanteros del Atlético, cinco goles en toda la temporada, quedan retratados en las dos últimas derrotas ante Bayern y Barça.
articles.summary: Los delanteros del Atlético, cinco goles en toda la temporada, quedan retratados en las dos últimas derrotas ante Bayern y Barça.
articles.body: Simeone acabó el partido ante el Barça buscando la remontada. En el verde, todo su arsenal ofensivo: Julián; Sorloth y Jonathan David. Ni un disparo a puerta pese a ello consiguió el Atlético en el segundo acto tras ser superior en la primera parte. Una dualidad curiosa que deja retratados a los tres hombres gol del equipo del Metropolitano. “Ellos sí tuvieron contundencia”, lamentaba el propio Cholo en las entrañas de un estadio que vio como su equipo superaba al líder durante el primer acto… antes de hundirse en el segundo. Se perdonaron ocasiones claras y se acabó pagando, en ese axioma que no suele fallar en el planeta fútbol. Y ahí aparece la figura de Julián. Era el día de la Araña por todo lo vivido en verano con el Barça y fue el jugador que salió más retratado. Estuvo activo, sí, pero falló dos ocasiones clarísimas de las que un delantero centro del primer escalón no suele perdonar. Dos ocasiones, una en cada parte, que molestaron a una grada que está en el proceso de perdonarle pero que todavía está lejos de hacerlo. Con dos goles este curso (ante Stuttgart y Deportivo), Simeone sigue buscando que aparezca el Julián de los picotazos de la primera temporada, pero el partido ante el Barça le aleja de ser la Araña que parecía predestinada a llevar la bandera rojiblanca durante muchos años. No se puede culpar únicamente a Julian del fracaso ofensivo rojiblanco. Sorloth ya había sido titular ante el Bayern y frente a los de Flick fue el primer cambio. Apenas inquieto pero quedó marcado por un ataque en el que se quedó parado ante un balón aéreo perfecto de Baena que le arrebató Cubarsí desde atrás. Un ejemplo perfecto de la indolencia que muestra el noruego en algunos lances y que sacó de quicio a parte del Metropolitano. Aunque no tuvo ocasiones claras, tampoco fue el día de un Jonathan David que empezó con buen pie de rojiblanco (tres partidos de Liga, tres goles) pero que se ha ido cayendo hasta ser el tercer delantero en la rotación. El canadiense no es el del arranque y frente al Barça vivió lejos del área, donde se diluye en su rendimiento. Los de Simeone llevaban 14 goles en siete partidos en casa (dos por partido). Estos dos partidos apenas han embocado uno en dos choques (0,5), es decir cuatro veces menos de producción ofensiva de los rojiblancos que han acabado en dos derrotas dolorosas. Seis puntos que han volado del fortín del Metropolitano mientras los 9 quedan retratados por su falta de acierto. No hay que olvidar que, más allá de estos dos partidos, apenas suman cinco goles entre los tres en toda la temporada. Balance global alejado de lo esperado tras 16 partidos entre Liga y Champions y que deberán revertir si no quieren que esa “falta de contundencia” se lleve por delante las opciones del Atlético de ganar algún título.

articles.title: Pau Cubarsí es el nuevo ‘chico de oro’
articles.standfirst: El central del Barcelona sucede a Désiré Doué y se corona como nuevo Golden Boy
articles.summary: El central del Barcelona sucede a Désiré Doué y se corona como nuevo Golden Boy
articles.body: España y el Barcelona ya tienen a su nuevo ‘chico de oro’. A sus 19 años, Pau Cubarsí (Estanyol, 2007) ha sido galardonado por el Diario ‘Tuttosport’ como Golden Boy 2026. El reconocimiento, sin duda, a la que fue su temporada de consagración en la máxima élite… culminada con la conquista de la Copa del Mundo. El canterano culé, que recogerá el premio en Turín en diciembre, acabó siendo el elegido como resultado de la votación en la que participaron medio centenar de periodistas provenientes de medios deportivos de toda Europa… entre los que se incluye MARCA, presente en el acto que ha tenido lugar en el MAPEI Football Center, ciudad deportiva del Sassuolo, con Demetrio Albertini como 'padrino' de lujo. Cada miembro del jurado podía votar por cinco futbolistas diferentes en orden descendente. Pau Cubarsí, de este modo, sucede a Désiré Doué (PSG/Francia) como el mejor futbolista europeo menor de 21 años. Es decir, aquellos nacidos a partir de 2006. Cabe resaltar que Lamine Yamal, compañero y compatriota, no podía ser reelegido, como ya sucedió en la pasada edición, al haber ganado el premio en 2024. Un criterio establecido por ‘Tuttosport’ desde que se comenzó a entregar este galardón allá por 2003. Entre la lista de 25 candidatos (20+5 ‘wild cards’) presentada por ‘Tuttosport’ a inicios del mes de octubre se encontraban otras estrellas emergentes como Ayyoub Bouaddi (Manchester City/Marruecos), Warren Zaïre-Emery (PSG/Francia), Yan Diomande (Real Madrid/Costa de Marfil) o Leenart Karl (Bayern Múnich/Alemania). Otros tres españoles acompañaban a Cubarsí entre los nominados: Jon Martín (Real Sociedad), Marc Bernal (Barcelona) y Xavi Espart (Barcelona). “Este premio tenía que ser para él”, llegó a pronunciar Lamine Yamal en la gala del Balón de Oro tras recibir su tercer Trofeo Kopa consecutivo. ‘Tuttosport’, sin embargo, sí ha tenido a bien reconocer la temporada de consagración definitiva vivida por un Pau Cubarsí que, a sus 19 años, ya se desempeña como un central curtido en mil batallas. Desde que Xavi Hernández le convirtiese en el sexto debutante más joven —actualmente, séptimo desde el estreno de Toni Fernández en 2025— en la historia del Barcelona, un 18 de enero de 2024 en Copa del Rey contra Unionistas, Cubarsí ha disputado 141 partidos con el primer equipo culé… a los que hay que sumarle otros 23 con la Selección. Pieza clave, sin duda, en la consecución de LaLiga, Supercopa y Mundial. Todos los ganadores del Golden Boy (2003 - 2026) La marcha de Iñigo Martínez le obligó a dar un paso al frente a nivel de responsabilidades, madurez y jerarquía que trasladó de manera excelsa al Mundial. Siempre elegante a la hora de generar superioridades desde el pase, consolidó un oficio defensivo impropio para un zaguero de su edad. Su intuición le hace tácticamente brillante, se siente cómodo defendiendo en la línea del centro del campo o protegiendo el área y no tiene ningún tipo de complejo a la hora de afrontar duelos. Disputó todos los minutos posibles y su pareja junto a Laporte fue la principal responsable de que España apenas recibiese un gol a lo largo del torneo. No en vano, fue elegido como el ‘Mejor Joven’ del Mundial. Para el recuerdo, el corte a centro de Giuliano en el área pequeña en dirección a Senesi para evitar que Argentina llevase la final a los penaltis. Siempre suele decirse “está llamado a dar muchas alegrías”. Este chico, sin embargo, ya lleva mucho tiempo haciéndolo. “Cuando el árbitro ha pitado el final, te das cuenta de que acabas de hacer historia”, analizaba sobre el césped del MetLife Stadium aquella noche del 19 de julio de 2026 un Pau Cubarsí que ahora recoge los frutos en forma de premio individual con este Golden Boy. Es, después de Matthijs de Ligt —central que más dinero ha movido en la historia— en 2018, el segundo defensor que ha conseguido ganar el premio. Ahora, su nombre pasa a estar escrito junto al de Cesc Fàbregas (2006), Isco Alarcón (2012), Pedri González (2021), Gavi (2022) y Lamine Yamal (2024). En total, a lo largo de estas 24 ediciones, ha habido seis ganadores —nadie tiene más— nacidos en España. Cuatro de ellos, además, han sido formados en La Masía y, a excepción de Isco, todos han vestido la camiseta del Barcelona. Una prueba más, por si aún no eran suficientes, de que no existe país mejor dotado a la hora de formar talento. El último, Pau Cubarsí: el nuevo ‘chico de oro’.

articles.title: CFP, ESPN Agree to Reported $1.7B Contract for Playoff Bracket Expansion, More Details Revealed
articles.summary: The 12-team playoff is dead. Long live the 24-team playoff.
articles.body:
The 12-team playoff is dead. Long live the 24-team playoff.

ESPN's Heather Dinich reported the College Football Playoff and ESPN agreed to a $1.7 billion deal that will see the postseason field expand ahead of the 2027 season.

As part of the arrangement, conference championship games for Power Four schools will end.

The top eight seeds will get a bye in the first round, up from four in the current format. There will also be an additional round of campus-site games.

Next season, the playoff field will be confirmed on Nov. 28, 2027. Meanwhile, the Heisman Trophy ceremony will now be moved up one week moving forward, with the Heisman weekend being held during December 3-5 in 2007.

This comes days after the CFP issued a statement saying a deal was "in the final stages of review." Monday's news doesn't come as a shock. The writing was on the wall.

Still, the new reality for college football is only beginning to sink in.

In broad terms, the sport hasn't changed dramatically since the inception of the playoff in 2014 and its subsequent expansion. The best teams got rewarded for their efforts, and winning your conference carried some importance.

A 24-team playoff is a dramatic recalibration.

Removing conference championships begs the question of what purpose a conference actually serves. The regular season will carry even less weight when a team can lose three games and still clinch a playoff berth. And making the playoff will become less of an achievement on its own.

A lot of fans rejoiced when college football ditched the BCS structure and adopted a true playoff. More than a decade on, it clearly wasn't the panacea some originally thought.

In due time, administrators may have to return to the negotiating table to debate over alterations to the 24-team postseason.

articles.title: Stephen Robinson: Aberdeen sack head coach with club 11th in Scottish Premiership after Hibs defeat
articles.summary: Aberdeen have parted ways with Robinson after their 4-0 loss to Hibernian; the Dons are second-bottom after just three wins from 12 Premiership games this season; the 51-year-old left St Mirren to take charge at Pittodrie in March; Stuart Duff placed in interim charge
articles.body:
It follows their 4-0 defeat to Hibernian on Saturday, which came just a week after the Pittodrie club lost their League Cup semi-final to Rangers.

The Dons have lost seven of their 12 Premiership matches this season, including four of their last five.

Fans inside Pittodrie called for his sacking during their defeat to Hibs, with the 51-year-old admitting the performance was not good enough, and ultimately bringing to an end his eight-month stint at the club.

Robinson joined from Scottish Premiership rivals St Mirren in March, signing a deal until the summer of 2029.

He arrived having led the Buddies to three consecutive top-six finishes, plus won the League Cup trophy in December. While he did save the club from the relegation play-offs last season, this season has seen not gone to plan.

Aberdeen say their search for a replacement is underway, with their first fixture following the international break away to Kilmarnock - who are directly below them in the Premiership - on November 21.

A club statement said: "Following a board meeting, Aberdeen Football Club has today taken the decision to part company with head coach Stephen Robinson.

"Stephen leaves the club alongside assistant head coach Brian Kerr and first team coach Stephen Craigan. We thank them for their efforts during their time at Pittodrie and wish them every success for the future.

"Preparatory work to support the appointment of a new manager has been undertaken, and the recruitment process is ongoing. The focus will be on identifying the right candidate to lead the club forward and deliver the progress expected across all areas of the football operation.

"Stuart Duff will assume interim charge of first team training while the club continues its search for a new Head Coach."

"It's not worked out the way that he [Robinson] would have thought it would have.

"Coming in last year and keeping Aberdeen in the league has got to be considered a success, but obviously they lost out in the semi-final last week and it's not been the start of the season that Aberdeen would have expected.

"I've got to be honest, I think there are a lot of other factors for me why the Stephen Robertson regime at Aberdeen hasn't worked.

"There are other people in there who have got to be held accountable as well.

"It's not been great for Aberdeen. They will tell you they're the third biggest team in the country, but right now, they're miles off it and they're going to have to start getting results."

articles.title: Real Madrid legend Raul appointed Real Oviedo manager
articles.summary: Former Real Madrid striker Raul takes on his first role in senior club management after being appointed as boss of Spanish second division side Real Oviedo.
articles.body:
Former Real Madrid striker Raul has taken on his first role in senior club management after being appointed , external as boss of Spanish second division side Real Oviedo.

The 49-year-old, who coached Real Madrid's reserves from 2019 to 2025, has signed a contract until June 2028.

Raul replaces Julian Calero, who was sacked by Oviedo on Monday with the side ninth in Spain's second division.

"My way of understanding football is with respecting the talent [in the squad] but asking for unconditional effort," said Raul in a video on Oviedo's social media.

"The team has to fight from the first minute to the last for victory so the fans are proud of them."

Raul enjoyed an illustrious playing career, helping Real Madrid win the Champions League three times and six La Liga titles.

He scored 323 goals in 741 games for the Bernabeu side before going on to play for Germany's Schalke, Al Sadd in Qatar, and American club New York Cosmos.

On the international front, Raul managed 44 goals in 102 games for Spain.

articles.title: Liverpool FC: Dominik Szoboszlai to have tests on knee injury before Nations League games against Georgia and Northern Ireland
articles.summary: Liverpool midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai will undergo tests on a knee injury to ascertain his readiness to join up with the Hungarian national side for Nations League fixtures against Georgia and Northern Ireland.
articles.body:
Liverpool midfielder Dominik Szoboszlai will undergo tests on a knee injury to ascertain his fitness for Hungary's Nations League fixtures against Georgia and Northern Ireland.

The 26-year-old was replaced after 69 minutes of the Anfield club's 3-1 Premier League victory over Crystal Palace on Sunday.

The Hungarian Football Federation have said their captain is "following the usual protocol in such cases" and that they will offer an update on his availability as soon as possible.

Hungary are second in Nations League Group B2, one point behind leaders Northern Ireland who they play in the concluding fixture of the campaign in Budapest on 17 November.

Before that potential decider, Marco Rossi's side travel to Georgia on Saturday.

Speaking after the win over Palace that lifted the Reds up to fourth in the Premier League table, Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola said he appreciates the player will do all he can to be available for his country.

"I know he will do everything to go because he loves to play with the national team, but he was not 100% when he finished the game.

"I suppose they will have to analyse, the medical staff, and see what it is.

"I know what I want, but I also have to understand the national teams. I'm sure that Dom, if he is fine he will want to go, but I'm not sure if he's going to be fine."

Szoboszlai, along with Alexander Isak and Cody Gakpo, missed Liverpool's 3-0 defeat by Manchester City in October directly following a four-game international window with Iraola keen to avoid any further stress on his playing squad.

"The last thing we need now is to lose players in the international games," he said.

"Last time, in the international break, we lost three very important players, so now I'm praying – it's the last thing we need.

"I think [Szoboszlai] extended a little bit the knee, it was fine, but not 100%, so he has to be careful to see if he can play with the national team or not."

articles.title: El amargo récord de Carrión: casi dos años y medio sin ganar
articles.standfirst: Encadena 22 partidos sin conocer la victoria como entrenador: ni en Primera, ni en Segunda ni en Copa del Rey
articles.summary: Encadena 22 partidos sin conocer la victoria como entrenador: ni en Primera, ni en Segunda ni en Copa del Rey
articles.body: ¿Mañana será el día? El Leganés de Luis Carrión se enfrenta al Trival Valderas en la Copa del Rey. Aunque los pepineros ejercerán de visitantes contra el equipo de Alcorcón, que milita en Tercera RFEF, el partido se disputará en Butarque. Si el equipo de Segunda división gana su partido y pasa de ronda, como es de esperar, Luis Carrión terminará con una sequía de casi dos años y medio sin ganar un partido. Concretamente, desde el 16 de junio de 2024, cuando su Real Oviedo derrotó al Espanyol (1-0) en la ida de la final de los playoffs. En el encuentro de vuelta, los pericos ganaron 2-0 y subieron a Primera. El técnico barcelonés salió del Tartiere y fichó por Las Palmas, de Primera división. Fueron 9 partidos en la isla antes de ser destituido, saldados con 6 derrotas y 3 empates. Un año después de su salida de la UD, regresó al equipo carbayón tras el despido de Paunovic. Tampoco ganó: 4 empates y 4 derrotas en Liga, además de la eliminación en Copa (4-2) contra el Ourense CF, de Primera RFEF. El 18 de octubre aterrizó en Leganés tras el cese de Rubén Albés. Arrancó su andadura con un empate contra el Mallorca (1-1), pero perdió los dos siguiente compromisos: 4-3 en Valladolid y 1-3 contra el Albacete. El equipo del sur de Madrid no gana desde el 20 de septiembre y está al borde de zona de descenso. En total son 22 partidos seguidos sin ganar o lo que es lo mismo, más de media Liga sin superar a un rival entre Primera, Segunda y Copa. ¿Acabará mañana la sequía?

articles.title: Mancini actualiza el posible 'fichaje' de Tresoldi por Italia: "Hay posibilidades"
articles.standfirst: El delantero del Brujas debe decidir entre Italia y Alemania
articles.summary: El delantero del Brujas debe decidir entre Italia y Alemania
articles.body: Apenas tiene 22 años y 'únicamente' juega en la liga belga, pero Nicolò Tresoldi vuelve a ser en este parón uno de los nombres de moda en el fútbol europeo. El delantero del Brujas, que lleva 14 goles en 17 partidos (cinco en Champions), debe decidir entre Italia y Alemania... aunque también podría jugar incluso por Argentina. De momento, el atacante está optando por Alemania Sub21... pero en Italia creen que pueden 'reclutarlo'. "Hablé con Tresoldi, Claudio Ranieri también lo hizo. Necesita sentir la necesidad de jugar para Italia, pero como nació en Italia y su padre también está en Italia, creo que hay posibilidades", declaraba Mancini, seleccionador 'azzurro'. Mientras, en Alemania, Klopp hace el mismo trabajo... para la 'Mannschaft'. La batalla entre germanos e italianos está servida... con Tresoldi, milanista, en el punto de mira de todos. Mancini, ya en Coverciano para el doble partido de Nations League ante Francia y Bélgica, continuó hablando sobre los jugadores con doble nacionalidad que podrían estar bajo escrutinio y llamada de la 'Nazionale'. "No somos solo nosotros, sino todas las selecciones nacionales. Intentamos fichar a aquellos con doble nacionalidad que sean buenos. Mientras tanto, logramos fichar a Palma, quien creo que puede convertirse en un muy buen defensa", declaraba. El joven central de Udinese fue llamado para este parón.

articles.title: The College Football Playoff is expanding to 24 teams. Football Saturdays will never be the same
articles.summary: College sports are becoming permanently bloated beyond recognition and meaningful college football Saturdays could become a thing of the past next year.
articles.body: There was a time, like all of a few months ago, when college football mastered the art of the regular season and college hoops solved the conundrum of the postseason. The magnitude of fall football Saturdays gave way to the madness of March, and – even if it was an imperfect split – both got something right. RIP to that. With the announcement that the College Football Playoff will expand to 24 teams, college athletics officially enters its Violet Beauregarde stage, engorged by gluttony just like the famed character from “Willy Wonka and the Chocolate Factory,” who essentially turned herself into a human blueberry. The Oompa Loompas eventually rolled poor Violet into the juicing room, squeezing her back to form, though leaving her permanently blue. There is no such quick fix for college athletics. It is permanently bloated almost beyond recognition. Beginning in 2027, a nice, even 100 Division I teams – 24 in football and 76 in hoops – will find their way into the postseason. A generation reared in the youth sports “everyone gets a trophy” era will now get their participation hardware even in college, and coaches can cash bonus checks for making a diluted bracket. The collateral damage? Meaningful college football Saturdays, fraught with the tension that a loss could be costly for a more selective playoff field. This past Saturday, Alabama whacked LSU and Utah claimed the Holy War, leaving the Tigers and BYU clinging by a fingernail to their playoff hopes. Next year, both likely survive for the first-round games between multi-loss teams that we once might have simply called the Poulan Weed-Eater Bowl. If college football wants a peek into its future, may we present college basketball? The sport has tried and failed for years to inject meaning into its early-season games. Good teams are doing a much better job of playing good teams early, but Virginia’s 19-point drubbing of Arkansas in November is the sports equivalent of a tree falling in the woods with no one around to hear it. What will it really matter come March? And now it really won’t matter. This spring, the beautiful basketball bracket will become but a bastardized version of itself. Similarly, middling power conference teams, given all of the resources and opportunities available but unable to win actual games, will instead be gifted a ticket to the ball. Meanwhile, Cinderella sits outside barefoot, wondering about the frauds scurrying around in their Manolo Blahniks. Because to be clear, this is not about expansion for the everyman and everywoman, the betterment of the game or a more engaging postseason. It is about money, pure and simple. The Athletic reported the expanded football playoff would be worth at least an additional $300 million and the bigger NCAA college basketball tournament an additional $50 million. Revenue sharing requires, believe it or not, revenue, and this is a way to not merely generate more of it, but to ensure that it is properly distributed. They’re called power conferences for a reason. The scales always tip in their favor and – when they don’t – a well-placed elbow can ensure that they do. The power brokers – the conference commissioners, university presidents, athletic directors, TV executives whose eyes cartoonishly pop like Scrooge McDuck’s with slot machine dollar signs, and the NCAA administrators who preferred the ostrich approach to an incoming earthquake – have crafted a model where the revenue is not shared; it is simply hoarded. Four Power 4 teams will be guaranteed spots in the new football playoff model, compared to just one reserved for the Group of Six. The NCAA Tournament, allegedly, will continue its meritocracy approach but anyone who thinks the Southern Conference is getting an extra bid over the SEC hasn’t been paying attention. Last year, 31 of the 37 at-large bids were split among the ACC, Big Ten, Big 12 and SEC. Even the Big East only received two. The rich will get richer, and the last shreds of college athletics being anything but minor-league stomping grounds will continue to erode into oblivion. The reality, and everyone in charge knows it, is that people will still go to games – regular season and postseason. And they will continue to watch. A quick and very unscientific survey of a few friends on a tailgating text chain offered what sounds like the general consensus among fans about the college football expanded playoff: No, I don’t want expansion, but if my team plays, I’ll go if I can and certainly watch. But it is also fair to question at what point fans start to feel like Violet: deflated and still blue. Extra playoff rounds and extra NCAA Tournament games mean more money – for tickets, for travel, for hotels – from fans who already are being asked to foot the bill for skyrocketing costs. The vicious cycle of revenue generation requires fans to pay more for tickets to attract better players so a team can win more games and thereby attract better players, who will then cost more money. That same text chain has bemoaned escalating prices across the board – for seats, for parking, for beer – with little return on their personal investment via current results on the field. Which is the one thing no one, not even the power-brokering power conferences, can manipulate. Whether the brackets include 24 teams or 76, only one ends up happy at the end. At what point does the juice not become worth the squeeze?

articles.title: Stephen Robinson: Aberdeen sack head coach after league slump
articles.summary: Aberdeen sack head coach Stephen Robinson after dropping to second bottom of the Scottish Premiership.
articles.body:
Stephen Robinson's Aberdeen reign is over inside eight months, with the head coach sacked after winning just three from 12 Premiership matches this season.

The Dons sit second bottom and Saturday's 4-0 home defeat by Hibernian was their fourth straight loss in all competitions.

Brian Kerr and Stephen Craigan have also left the club, with Stuart Duff placed in interim charge.

Club hero Willie Miller described Saturday's result as "utterly embarrassing", going on to tell BBC Sportsound listeners that Robinson resembled "a man lost".

The 51-year-old former Northern Ireland international previously managed Oldham Athletic, Motherwell, Morecambe and St Mirren.

On the back of three successive top-six finishes and a League Cup triumph, Robinson left the Paisley side for Aberdeen in March, agreeing a contract until the summer of 2029.

The sixth permanent manager since Dave Cormack took control at Pittodrie in November 2019, he steered the Dons away from relegation trouble last term before overhauling the squad with 15 signings.

Across 28 games in all competitions, Robinson departs with a record of 11 wins, five draws and 12 defeats.

The next manager will inherit a squad low on confidence, the joint lowest scorers in the league.

Robinson chopped and changed between four and five at the back but that yielded just two top-flight clean sheets.

Of the plethora of summer recruits, only goalkeeper Marius Muller and full-back Nesta Guinness-Walker have played in every league game.

Top scorer Kevin Nisbet is the other player to have done the same and scunnered fans cheered when the captain was replaced at the weekend.

"The players aren't up to scratch, not up to playing at this level and dealing with high-ish expectations," was the damning assessment from Miller.

"I'm not talking about trophies, I'm talking about being in the top six and they're nowhere near that."

After the international break, Aberdeen travel to face Kilmarnock on 21 November then visit Rangers three days later before their next home game against Dundee on 28 November.

Former Aberdeen captain, manager & director Willie Miller

You are looking at 15 payers out and 15 players in, so it is a huge turnaround of players, was that all Stephen Robinson? I would imagine probably yes but I don't know because I am not privy to that information.

But at the same time, when you make that amount of changes, when you have assessed the squad and to be fair on Stephen as well he came in at a very uncertain time and relegation perhaps staring the club in the face so he managed initially to get the performances with the players he inherited.

But then you make all the changes with the support from the board, you bring all these new players in and I think there was never a stable formation either.

The board have really worked hard over the years to try and get Aberdeen back to a kind of level, won a cup a couple of years ago. I don't blame the board for anything at all.

Recruitment is absolutely key and if you've bought a bunch of players and then they're not performing then that is a real worry. There's a few players in there that are already at a good level but can the others jump on that wagon and get Aberdeen rolling again because it's a very difficult time for them.

I'm not going to criticise the players because I'm not really sure what level they're at. You have to be a fairly good level to be in the Aberdeen team and to get back to that kind of level is going to be tough.

Analysis: 'Robinson swimming against tide from start'

The phrase rinse and repeat may apply to hair washing, but these days it also applies to Aberdeen's recruitment of managers.

While no-one can fault the commitment chairman Dave Cormack has shown to the club during his tenure, the managerial success rate under his stewardship is low - and that is probably putting a positive spin on things.

For the Dons, this procedure feels like a movie that has had a number of disappointing sequels.

Barring last year's Scottish Cup win, there has been a general downward trajectory in fortunes for Aberdeen. Undoubtedly, the constant chopping and changing has been a huge factor.

As for Robinson - it felt like he has been swimming against the North Sea tide since his appointment.

He came in after a protracted search to find Jimmy Thelin's successor and his appointment was not greeted with much approval from the Red Army, who viewed it as one driven more by panic than anything else.

The frustration and disgruntlement among the Aberdeen support has only grown, one which has certainly felt like it has long gone past any tipping point.

Robinson has cut a beleaguered figure in the dugout, and post-match interviews during the dying embers of his tenure were difficult.

Now it is over to recently appointed chief executive Adrian Bevington.

Much has been made of the network of contacts both Bevington and sporting director Lutz Pfannenstiel possess.

Those will be needed as they aim to make an appointment whose first priority will be to stop an alarming slide that is threatening to plunge them in to the darkest of relegation mires.

articles.title: FIFPRO World 11: Ballon d'Or winner Harry Kane not voted by fellow professionals to be named in team of the year
articles.summary: Harry Kane becomes the first Ballon d'Or winner to not be named in the FIFPRO World 11 after claiming the award; England team-mate Jude Bellingham is included; seven WSL stars have made the Women's FIFPRO World 11
articles.body:
Over 18,000 professional footballers have chosen their best men's team, with the final 11 being chosen from a group of 26 selected finalists.

Kane, who won the Ballon d'Or ahead of Real Madrid's Kylian Mbappe by one of the smallest margins in history, was among the 26 finalists but did not make the final team.

Mbappe, Manchester City's Erling Haaland, Barcelona's Lamine Yamal and Inter Miami's Lionel Messi were named in a Kane-less front four, which also excluded Cristiano Ronaldo and Michael Olise.

Kane became the first English Ballon d'Or winner last month since Michael Owen in 2001, and only the fifth in history following in the footsteps Sir Stanley Matthews, Sir Bobby Charlton, Kevin Keegan and Owen.

The Bayern Munich star received just 27.6 per cent of votes of all the forwards, with Haaland marginally bettering him at 28.4 per cent. It is the first time since the award's inception in 2005 that the Ballon d'Or winner has not been selected for the XI.

Kane's international team-mate, Jude Bellingham, was named in midfield alongside Barcelona star Rodri and PSG's Vitinha.

Arsenal's David Raya was named in goal, with Pau Cubarsi, Achraf Hakimi and Nuno Mendes rounding things out in a back three.

Goalkeeper: David Raya (Arsenal & Spain)

Defenders: Achraf Hakimi (PSG & Morocco), Pau Cubarsi (Barcelona & Spain), Nuno Mendes (PSG & Portugal)

Midfielders: Vitinha (PSG & Portugal), Rodri (Man City/Barcelona & Spain), Jude Bellingham (Real Madrid & England)

Forwards: Lamine Yamal (Barcelona & Spain), Erling Haaland (Man City & Norway), Lionel Messi (Inter Miami & Argentina), Kylian Mbappe (Real Madrid & France).

SEVEN WSL stars named in FIFPRO World 11

Seven players from the WSL have been named in the 2026 Women's FIFPRO World 11.

Over 6,500 women's footballers from 64 countries voted for their team of the year, which also included five of Sarina Wiegman's Lionesses.

Lucy Bronze earned a record-breaking ninth appearance in the XI, and is joined by Chelsea team-mate, goalkeeper Hannah Hampton.

Manchester City's Alex Greenwood also features in a backline that sees London City Lionesses defender Mapi Leon included.

Manchester United's Ella Toone joins a midfield that includes Ballon d'Or winner Alexia Putellas and three-time recipient Aitana Bonmati. Arsenal striker Alessia Russo rounds out the WSL inclusions.

Barcelona defender Irene Paredes, forward Claudia Pina and Orlando Pride's Barbra Banda complete the XI.

Goalkeeper: Hannah Hampton (Chelsea & England)

Defenders: Lucy Bronze (Chelsea & England), Alex Greenwood (Man City & England), Mapi Leon (Barcelona/London City Lionesses & Spain), Irene Paredes (Barcelona & Spain)

Midfielders: Aitana Bonmati (Barcelona & Spain), Alexia Putellas (Barcelona/London City Lionesses & Spain), Ella Toone (Man Utd & England)

Forwards: Barbra Banda (Orlando Pride & Zambia), Claudia Pina (Barcelona & Spain), Alessia Russo (Arsenal & England).

articles.title: Norway v Wales: Leeds United's Harry Wilson eyes Nation League survival boost
articles.summary: Harry Wilson believes Wales can shock Norway again in Oslo on Saturday and move a step closer to survival in Nations League A.
articles.body:
Harry Wilson believes Wales can shock Norway again in Oslo on Saturday and move a step closer to survival in Nations League A.

Wales upset Erling Haaland and company in Cardiff last month to register a first ever win in the Nations League's top tier.

Craig Bellamy's side know another success in the return fixture would be a major boost to their hopes of remaining among Europe's elite.

As it stands, Wales are third in Group A4, above Norway based on their head-to-head record.

However, another win this weekend would not be enough to guarantee Wales finish third or better – and in doing so improve their Euro 2028 qualification prospects – because they could conceivably end the group with the same number of points as Norway and Denmark.

Should that happen, they would be separated by goal difference in the games involving those three sides.

For the moment, however, Wilson says all eyes are on toppling the Norwegians.

"I feel like we know what we've got to do on Saturday to keep us in Group A and it's full focus and full steam ahead to do that," the attacking midfielder said.

Live on BBC iPlayer, BBC Two Wales, BBC Sounds, BBC Radio Wales, Radio Cymru and 5 Live Sports Extra, BBC Sport website and app, plus live text commentary.

"I think [the target] before we started this campaign was to try to remain in Group A.

"It's what we've worked so hard to do and to play against the best teams in Europe and ultimately down the line when the qualifying games start, it puts us in a better position the better we do in this group.

"I think a win on Saturday gives us a good chance of staying in Group A and then we have the massive game against Portugal on Tuesday [17 November], so ultimately the focus is on getting a win in Oslo on Saturday."

Wales could still finish in second, third or fourth place in their group.

A top-two spot would take Craig Bellamy's side to the Nations League quarter-finals in March 2027.

Finishing third would mean a relegation play-off against a League B team in March, while finishing bottom of the group would result in either a relegation play-off or direct relegation, depending on the ranking with other League A groups.

Crucially, finishing either second or third would mean Wales are seeded in the draw for the next European Championship.

Raya, Pickford and Wales' search for a new keeper

Wilson returns as Wales call up uncapped Duncan

The return of attacking midfielder Wilson is a significant boost for Bellamy's squad as they look to end a challenging Nations League campaign on a high.

The 29-year-old is yet to feature in the group having missed the four-game international window in September and October because of a muscle injury.

Wilson says he was "absolutely gutted" to pick up the fitness issue just before the previous international camp.

"Whoever came up with that four-game win, he needs sacking," he said with a smile.

"You get an injury a couple of days before that and it rules you up for four games and you should only miss two. Whoever's come up with that, it cost me another four games.

"For me personally, I'm itching to get back out there."

Wilson is with the national squad for the first time as a Leeds United player.

With his Fulham contract up, Wilson signed for the Yorkshire club on a free transfer in July, joining fellow countrymen Joe Rodon, Ethan Amapdu, Daniel James and Jayden Lienou at Elland Road.

After a spectacular final season at Fulham, during which he was a first-team regular and scored 11 club goals, Wilson has had to be patient at Leeds.

He has made only three Premier League starts so far Leeds – as well as five substitute appearances – and is yet to score for his new club, who are currently ninth in the top flight.

"When I wasn't in the team, the team was doing well," Wilson said.

"I'm an honest player and I understand when I've been in starting XIs, and in teams where I'm doing well, I don't want to be dropped.

"But more recently, wins have started to be a little bit more difficult to come by and I've started a few more games. I think that's how football is.

"I'm a player that wants to play every game, but ultimately it's the manager's decision and the players who do play have to perform to stay in the team."

articles.title: Aprendamos de los errores
articles.standfirst: Jesús Velasco no quiso provocar un terremoto, simplemente reivindicó el trabajo que se hace en el fútbol sala español y aprovechó el escaparate tras conquistar la 'Finalissima'
articles.summary: Jesús Velasco no quiso provocar un terremoto, simplemente reivindicó el trabajo que se hace en el fútbol sala español y aprovechó el escaparate tras conquistar la 'Finalissima'
articles.body: Una expresión como "es una vergüenza que Teledeporte no haya televisado esto", pronunciadas por Jesús Velasco, en la zona mixta del Arena de Niterói, con presencia de los medios oficiales de la Federación, Futsalia y varios medios y periodistas brasileños y de otros países, ha provocado un terremoto entre las celebraciones de la selección y el regreso del combinado nacional a nuestro país. Cierto es que Jesús Velasco quizás debería haber sido más políticamente correcto en ese momento y haber dicho algo así como "es una vergüenza que ningún canal español, excepción la propia RFEF en su canal de Youtube, haya televisado la competición. Pero lo dicho, dicho está. Creo que, como en el resto de sus palabras, Jesús Velasco quiso aprovechar el gran momento que vive la Selección española de fútbol sala para reivindicar un deporte, el suyo, el fútbol sala, y a cuantos, encabezados por los jugadores que lo practican, terminando en los aficionados, necesitan que en esos momentos en que los focos estén centrados en el fútbol sala, levanten la voz. El fútbol sala es uno de los deportes más ninguneados en el panorama deportivo mundial. El hecho de que sea, relativamente parecido, pero disputarse en 40x20 metros, puede que le haya convertido en un 'minifútbol' que no merece que la Carta Olímpica lo incluya entre los que se disputan habitualmente en los Juegos Olímpicos y que se van ampliando según sea la ciudad que los acoge. El trabajo que se hace en fútbol sala en nuestro país es ingente. Muchas veces lejos de los focos mediáticos y Jesús Velasco se ha acordado de ellos de todos los que lo hacen posible todos y cada uno de los días en todas y cada una de las localidades. Otra cosa es el tema de la retransmisión de la competición. Ahora mismo el fútbol sala se puede ver en abierto en los canales de RTVE (Teledeporte-o RTVE Play, aunque cuesta a ciertos aficionados ver deporte en las aplicaciones) y en cerrado en DAZN la Liga Prime Futsal. Teledeporte siempre ha tenido una especial sensibilidad con el 40x20, pero en esta ocasión algo ha fallado. Es posible que las exigencias de la UEFA y la Conmebol, que organizaban la competición, no haya podido ser satisfecha por el ente, pero ahí queda para próximas ocasiones. Sin ningún género de dudas la Selección española, que desde el 1 de noviembre de 2024, dirige Jesús Velasco es ahora, como siempre ha sido, el gran escaparate del fútbol sala español. Sirva este apagón televisivo para recordar que hay infinidad de deportes que nunca tendrán la repercusión en cuotas de audiencia del fútbol, por ejemplo, pero sí que despiertan el interés de los aficionados porque, hoy en día, lo que no se ve parece que no existe.
